45-Degree Hip Extension: Rest your hips on the pad with ankles locked under the rollers, body hanging forward. Hinge up by squeezing your glutes until your body is level, then lower slowly. Rounding your lower back to rise is the common fault.
Ab Crunch Machine: Sit in the machine with the pad across your chest and hips still. Curl your ribs down towards your hips rather than nodding your head forward. Pulling with the neck instead of curling the torso is the usual fault.
Abduction Machine: Sit with your back flat and the outside of your knees against the pads. Push your knees apart against the machine, then bring them back slowly. Rocking your hips to help the push is the common fault.
Assisted Dip Machine: Kneel on the platform with the counterweight set to support part of your weight, hands on the bars. Lower by bending your elbows until your shoulders dip, then press back up. Flaring the elbows wide takes the work off the chest.
Assisted Pull-Up: Kneel on the platform with the counterweight set to offset your weight, and take an overhand grip above you. Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows down, then lower slowly. Letting the machine do all the work wastes the rep.
Back Extension (Weighted): Set your hips on the pad with ankles locked under the rollers, holding a plate to your chest. Hinge forward until you feel a stretch, then squeeze your glutes to rise level. Rounding your lower back on the way down is the usual fault.
Bayesian Curl: Stand facing away from a low pulley with your arm extended behind your torso. Curl the handle up towards your shoulder, keeping the elbow pinned behind you. Letting the elbow drift forward loses the stretch that makes this curl useful.
Belt Squat: Clip the belt around your hips and stand on the platform with the weight hanging below. Bend your knees and hips to lower until your thighs are level, then drive back up. Letting your knees cave inward on the way up is the common fault.
Bent-Over Cable Rear Delt Fly: Stand facing a low cable and hinge forward from the hips with soft knees. Sweep both arms out and back in an arc, leading with your elbows, then return slowly. Heaving the weight with your back instead of your shoulders is the common fault.
Cable Anti-Rotation Hold (Half-Kneeling): Kneel on one knee side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle with both hands out in front. Press the handle out and hold it there, resisting the pull towards the machine. Letting your hips twist open defeats the hold.
Cable Behind-the-Back Shrug: Stand facing away from a low cable, holding the handle behind your hips with straight arms. Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears, then lower slowly. Rolling the shoulders back instead of lifting straight up is the usual fault.
Cable Chest Press (Standing): Stand in a split stance facing away from the machine, a handle in each hand at chest height. Press both handles forward until your arms extend, then return slowly. Leaning your whole body forward to help the press is the common fault.
Cable Concentration Curl: Stand or sit side-on to a low pulley, bracing your arm against your inner thigh. Curl the handle up towards your shoulder without swinging the elbow, then lower slowly. Letting the elbow drift off your leg turns this into a swing.
Cable Crossover (High to Low): Set both pulleys above head height, a handle in each hand, leaning slightly forward. Pull both handles down and together in front of your hips, squeezing your chest. Bending the elbows too much turns the fly into a press.
Cable Crunch: Kneel below a high pulley holding a rope beside your head, hips stacked over your knees. Curl your ribs down towards your hips, then let the weight pull you back up. Bending only at the hips instead of the spine misses the abs.
Cable Curl: Stand facing a low pulley with a bar attached, elbows pinned to your sides. Curl the bar up towards your shoulders without the elbows drifting forward, then lower slowly. Swinging your torso to start the curl is the common fault.
Cable Donkey Kickback: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley, face the machine, and lean forward slightly for balance. Kick the leg back and up, squeezing the glute at the top, then return slowly. Arching your back for extra height takes work off the glute.
Cable Face Pull: Set a rope at head height and step back for tension, arms out in front. Pull it towards your face, splitting the ends and elbows wide, then return slowly. Pulling straight into the chest instead of splitting the rope misses the rear delts.
Cable Face Pull (Rope): Attach a rope at head height and step back so the cable is taut, arms out in front. Pull it apart towards your face, elbows high and wide, then return slowly. Shrugging your shoulders instead of drawing the elbows back is the usual fault.
Cable Face Pull (Upper Back): Set a rope at head height and step back with tension in the cable, palms facing each other. Pull it towards your forehead, elbows back and down, squeezing your upper back. Letting the elbows rise too high turns this into a shoulder move.
Cable Fly (Chest Height): Set both pulleys level with your chest, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Bring your hands together in a wide arc in front of your chest, then open back out slowly. Bending the elbows more as it gets hard turns this into a press.
Cable Fly (High to Low): Set both pulleys above head height, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Sweep your hands down and together towards your hips, feeling the stretch across your chest. Letting the handles drift towards your face misses the target.
Cable Fly (Low to High): Set both pulleys low, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Sweep your hands up and together in front of your upper chest, then return down and out. Using your legs to throw the handles up takes the work off the chest.
Cable Fly (Neutral): Set both pulleys level with your chest, palms facing each other throughout. Sweep your hands together in a wide arc in front of your chest, then open back out slowly. Letting your wrists rotate during the movement is the common fault.
Cable Front Raise: Stand facing away from a low pulley, the handle held in front of your thighs, elbows softly bent. Raise the handle straight out to roughly shoulder height, then lower slowly. Heaving the weight up with your lower back is the common fault.
Cable Hammer Curl (Rope): Stand facing a low pulley with a rope attached, palms facing each other. Curl the rope up towards your shoulders with elbows pinned to your sides, then lower slowly. Letting the elbows swing forward turns this into a shoulder move.
Cable High Row: Set the pulley above shoulder height and stand back, holding the handle at arm's length. Pull it towards your upper chest, elbows back and up, then extend slowly. Shrugging your shoulders towards your ears is the common fault.
Cable Hip Abduction: Sit in the machine or attach an ankle strap to a low pulley, bracing with your hands. Push the working leg out to the side against it, then bring it back slowly. Leaning your torso away to help the leg move is the common fault.
Cable Hip Adduction: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley out to the side, standing with the working leg out wide. Pull the leg across your body against it, then let it return slowly. Rotating your hips instead of moving the leg straight is the usual fault.
Cable Iron Cross: Set both pulleys low and stand between them, arms extended out to the sides holding a handle each. Pull both handles up and across to meet in front of your chest, then return slowly. Bending the elbows too early turns this into a curl.
Cable Kickback: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and face the machine, hinging forward slightly with a flat back. Drive the leg back and up, squeezing the glute, then lower slowly. Arching your back for range takes work off the glute.
Cable Kickback (Triceps): Stand facing away from a low pulley with your elbow pinned high and close to your body. Extend your forearm back until your arm straightens, then return slowly. Letting the elbow drop as you extend takes the tension off the triceps.
Cable Lat Pullover: Lie on a bench facing away from a high pulley, arms extended overhead holding a straight bar. Pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs, elbows slightly bent, then return slowly. Bending the elbows more turns this into a pulldown.
Cable Lateral Raise: Stand beside a low pulley with the cable crossing your body, arm hanging by your hip. Raise your arm out to shoulder height, leading with the elbow, then lower slowly. Shrugging your shoulder up is the common fault.
Cable Lateral Raise (Behind the Back): Stand with the cable set low behind you, running to your working hand. Raise your arm out to shoulder height, then lower slowly for the extra stretch. Shrugging the shoulder instead of leading with the elbow is the usual fault.
Cable Overhead Bicep Curl: Set the pulley high, raise your arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent. Curl your hand towards your head, keeping your upper arm still, then extend back out. Dropping the elbow instead of holding it in place is the common fault.
Cable Overhead Tricep Extension: Stand facing away from a low pulley with a rope held behind your head, elbows pointing forward. Extend your arms forward and up until they straighten, then return slowly. Letting the elbows flare out to the sides takes work off the triceps.
Cable Pull-Through: Face away from a low pulley with a rope between your legs and hinge forward. Drive your hips forward to standing, squeezing your glutes, then hinge back slowly. Squatting the weight up instead of hinging is the usual fault.
Cable Pull-Through (Glute): Face away from a low pulley with a rope between your legs and hinge forward until you feel a stretch. Drive your hips forward hard, pausing to squeeze your glutes. Bending your knees to squat the weight up is the common fault.
Cable Pushdown (Straight Bar): Stand facing a high pulley with a straight bar attached, elbows tucked to your sides. Push the bar down until your arms straighten, then let it rise slowly. Letting the elbows drift away from your body is the common fault.
Cable Rear Delt Fly: Stand between two low pulleys, crossing the handles to opposite hands, leaning slightly forward. Sweep your arms out and back to shoulder height, then return slowly. Heaving with your back instead of your rear delts is the usual fault.
Cable Reverse Curl: Stand facing a low pulley with an overhand grip, elbows tucked to your sides. Curl the handle up towards your shoulders keeping your wrists firm, then lower fully. Letting the wrists bend during the curl takes tension off the forearms.
Cable Reverse Curl (Forearms): Stand facing a low pulley with an overhand grip, elbows pinned to your sides. Curl up keeping your wrists straight and firm, then lower slowly. Letting the wrists flick forward is the common fault.
Cable Reverse Woodchop (Kneeling): Kneel side-on to a low pulley, holding the handle with both hands near your hip. Pull it diagonally up and across your body, rotating through your torso, then return slowly. Using only your arms instead of rotating is the usual fault.
Cable Reverse Wrist Curl: Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing down, holding the handle loosely. Curl your wrist up towards you, then lower it fully slowly. Using your forearm instead of just the wrist is the common fault.
Cable Reverse-Grip Pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pads, take an underhand grip on the bar, arms extended overhead. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, elbows down and back, then return slowly. Leaning back excessively is the usual fault.
Cable Rope Hammer Curl: Stand facing a low pulley holding a rope with a neutral grip, elbows tucked to your sides. Curl the rope up towards your shoulders, then lower fully slowly. Letting the elbows swing forward once it gets harder is the common fault.
Cable Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown (Single: Sit or kneel facing a high pulley with a rope in one hand, arm extended overhead. Pull the rope down to your hip, keeping your arm straight, then return slowly. Bending the elbow to help pull turns this into a pushdown.
Cable Row (Wide Grip): Sit with your feet on the platform and take a wide bar, arms extended with a tall spine. Pull the bar towards your torso with elbows out wide, then extend back out slowly. Rounding your back at the start is the common fault.
Cable Shrug: Stand facing a low pulley with the handle held at your hips, arms straight. Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears, then lower slowly. Rolling the shoulders instead of moving straight up and down is the common fault.
Cable Side Bend: Stand side-on to a low pulley holding the handle at your hip. Bend sideways away from the machine, then pull back up to standing using your side abs. Twisting your torso instead of bending straight sideways is the usual fault.
Cable Squat (Standing): Face a low pulley with the handle held at your chest with both hands, feet shoulder width apart. Squat down keeping your chest up, then drive back up through your heels. Letting your knees cave inward on the way up is the common fault.
Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown: Stand facing a high pulley with a straight bar held at arm's length, a slight bend in the elbows. Pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs, then let it rise slowly. Bending the elbows more as it comes down turns this into a pushdown.
Cable Upright Row: Stand facing a low pulley with an overhand grip on the bar, arms hanging in front. Pull the bar up towards your chin, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. Shrugging instead of leading with the elbows is the common fault.
Cable Upright Row (Traps): Stand facing a low pulley with a close overhand grip. Pull the bar up towards your chin, leading with your elbows and shrugging at the top, then lower slowly. A wide grip instead of a close one shifts work off the traps.
Cable Woodchop: Stand side-on to a high pulley, holding the handle with both hands away from your body. Pull it down and across your body, rotating through your torso, then return slowly. Using only your arms instead of your core is the common fault.
Cable Woodchop (Half-Kneeling): Kneel on the outside knee side-on to a high pulley, holding the handle with both hands. Pull the handle down and across your body, rotating through your torso, then return slowly. Letting the back knee lift off the floor is the usual fault.
Cable Woodchop (High to Low): Stand side-on to a high pulley, holding the handle away from your body. Pull it down and across your body in a diagonal line, rotating through your torso, then return slowly. Using only your arms instead of your core is the fault.
Cable Woodchop (Low to High): Stand side-on to a low pulley, holding the handle near your hip. Pull it up and across your body in a diagonal line, rotating through your torso, then return slowly. Standing too square instead of rotating fully is the usual fault.
Cable Wrist Curl: Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing up, holding the handle at your fingertips. Curl your wrist up towards you, then lower it fully to stretch the forearm. Moving your elbow instead of your wrist is the common fault.
Cable Y-Raise (Prone): Lie face down on an incline bench holding light handles below you, arms straight. Raise your arms up and out to form a Y shape, squeezing your upper back, then lower slowly. Bending the elbows to cheat the weight up is the common fault.
Cable Y-Raise (Standing): Stand facing away from two low pulleys, a handle in each hand at your hips. Raise both arms up and out into a Y shape above your head, then lower slowly. Shrugging instead of raising through the arms is the common fault.
Chest Press Machine (Single-Arm): Sit in the machine with one handle at chest height, feet flat on the floor. Press the handle forward until your arm extends, then return slowly without twisting your torso. Rotating your body to help the press is the common fault.
Cross-Body Cable Tricep Extension: Stand side-on to a low pulley, holding the handle across your body with your elbow bent. Extend your arm down and across your body until it straightens, then return slowly. Letting the elbow drift away from your side is the common fault.
Decline Machine Press: Sit in the machine with the seat adjusted so the handles sit level with your lower chest. Press the handles forward and slightly down until your arms extend, then return slowly. Flaring the elbows out wide is the common fault.
Dip Machine: Set your grip on the handles with your body upright or leaning slightly forward. Lower your body by bending your elbows, then press back up to straight arms. Leaning too far forward shifts the work onto the chest instead of the triceps.
Donkey Calf Raise (Machine): Stand in the machine with your hips against the pad and the balls of your feet on the platform. Rise onto your toes as high as possible, pause, then lower for a full stretch. Bouncing through a short range is the usual fault.
Donkey Kickback (Machine): Kneel in the machine with your knee under the pad and your foot pressed against the lever. Drive your leg back and up, squeezing the glute at the top, then return slowly. Arching your lower back for extra height takes work off the glute.
Face Pull: Set a rope at head height and step back for tension, arms out in front. Pull it towards your face, splitting the ends and driving your elbows wide, then return slowly. Pulling low into the chest instead of high misses the target.
Face Pull (Rope): Attach a rope at head height and step back so the cable is taut, arms extended in front. Pull it apart towards your face, keeping your elbows high, then return slowly. Letting the elbows drop low turns this into a row.
Face Pull (Traps): Set a rope at head height and step back with tension in the cable. Pull it towards your face while shrugging your shoulders up at the finish, then lower slowly. Skipping the shrug at the top misses the traps.
GHD Sit-Up: Lie back on the GHD with your hips supported and feet locked under the footplates. Curl your torso up until you are upright, then lower back down slowly. Swinging up with momentum instead of curling through the abs is the common fault.
Glute Ham Raise: Kneel with your ankles locked under the footplates, body upright to start. Lower your torso forward slowly by fighting the fall with your hamstrings, then curl back up. Bending at the hips instead of the knees takes work off the hamstrings.
Glute Kickback Machine: Kneel in the machine with one knee on the pad and your foot pressed against the lever. Drive the leg back and up, squeezing the glute at the top, then return slowly. Rushing the reps without a pause at the top is the common fault.
Glute-Ham Raise Machine: Kneel with your ankles locked under the footplates, body upright. Curl forward and back using your hamstrings to control the movement, then return upright. Letting your hips lead the movement instead of your hamstrings is the usual fault.
Hack Squat Machine: Set your shoulders and back against the pads, feet shoulder width apart on the platform. Bend your knees to lower until your thighs are roughly level, then drive back up. Letting your knees cave inward as you push up is the common fault.
Half-Kneeling Cable Row: Kneel on one knee facing a low pulley, the other foot forward, holding the handle at arm's length. Pull the handle towards your ribs, driving your elbow back, then extend slowly. Twisting your torso to help the pull is the common fault.
Half-Kneeling Pallof Press: Kneel on one knee side-on to a cable at chest height, the handle held with both hands against your chest. Press it straight out and hold, without letting your torso twist. Letting your hips or shoulders rotate open defeats the hold.
Hammer Strength Chest Press: Sit in the machine with the handles at chest height and your feet flat on the floor. Press the handles forward until your arms extend, then return slowly. Bouncing the handles off your chest at the bottom is the common fault.
Hand Gripper: Hold the gripper in one hand with the handles resting in your palm and fingers. Squeeze the handles together until they touch, then release slowly under control. Using short, fast squeezes instead of a full close is the common fault.
High Cable Curl: Stand between two high pulleys with a handle in each hand, arms out at shoulder height. Curl both hands towards your head, keeping your upper arms still, then extend back out. Dropping the elbows during the curl is the common fault.
High Cable Fly: Set both pulleys above head height, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Pull your hands down and together in front of your hips, squeezing your lower chest. Letting the handles rise towards your face misses the target.
Hip Adduction Machine: Sit with your back against the pad and the inside of your knees against the pads. Squeeze your knees together against the machine, then let them return slowly. Using your hands to help pull the pads together is the common fault.
Hip Extension (Cable): Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley, face the machine, and hold on with a flat back. Drive the working leg straight back and up, squeezing the glute, then return slowly. Arching your lower back for extra height takes work off the glute.
Hyperextension (Back Extension): Set your hips on the pad with ankles locked under the rollers, body hanging forward. Hinge forward until you feel a stretch, then squeeze your glutes to rise level. Rounding your lower back on the way down is the usual fault.
Incline Cable Chest Press: Lie back on an incline bench facing away from low pulleys, a handle in each hand at chest height. Press both handles up and forward until your arms extend, then return slowly. Letting the handles drift towards your face is the common fault.
Incline Cable Fly: Lie back on an incline bench between two low pulleys, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Bring your hands together above your chest in a wide arc, then open back out slowly. Bending the elbows more turns this into a press.
Incline Machine Press: Sit in the machine with the seat set so the handles sit level with your upper chest. Press the handles forward and slightly up until your arms extend, then return slowly. Flaring the elbows out wide is the common fault.
Incline Smith Machine Press: Set a bench to a moderate incline under the bar, lie back, and unhook it by rotating your wrists. Lower the bar to your upper chest, then press back up to straight arms. Setting the bench too steep turns this into a shoulder press.
Iso-Lateral Chest Press: Sit in the machine with a handle in each hand at chest height, feet flat on the floor. Press each handle forward independently until your arms extend, then return slowly. Letting one arm lead the other throws off the balance of the press.
Iso-Lateral Front Pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pads and grip a handle in each hand above you. Pull both handles down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down, then extend slowly. Leaning back too far to help the pull is the common fault.
Kneeling Cable Crunch: Kneel below a high pulley holding a rope beside your head, hips stacked over your knees. Curl your ribs down towards your hips, then let the weight pull you back up. Bending at the hips instead of the spine misses the abs.
Lat Pulldown (Close Grip): Sit with your thighs under the pads and take a close grip on the handle above you. Pull the handle down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down, then extend slowly. Leaning back excessively to help the pull is the usual fault.
Lat Pulldown (Neutral Grip): Sit with your thighs under the pads and take a neutral grip on the handles above you. Pull the handles down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down, then extend slowly. Using momentum from leaning back is the common fault.
Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip): Sit with your thighs under the pads and take a wide overhand grip on the bar above you. Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down and out, then extend slowly. Pulling the bar behind your neck is the usual fault.
Lateral Raise Machine: Sit with your back against the pad and your upper arms against the outer pads. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, then lower slowly. Shrugging instead of raising through the arms is the common fault.
Leaning Cable Lateral Raise: Hold onto a post and lean your body away from a low pulley on the other side. Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, leading with the elbow, then lower slowly. Standing upright instead of leaning away limits the stretch.
Leg Curl (Cable): Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and stand facing the machine, holding on for balance. Curl your heel up towards your glute against the resistance, then lower slowly. Swinging your hips to help the curl is the common fault.
Leg Extension: Sit with your back against the pad and the pad resting on top of your shins. Extend your legs until they straighten, pause, then lower slowly. Swinging the weight up with momentum instead of a controlled extension is the common fault.
Leg Press: Sit with your back flat against the pad, feet shoulder width apart on the platform. Bend your knees to lower the platform towards you, then press back up without locking hard. A rounding lower back off the pad is the common fault.
Leg Press (High Foot): Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet set high on the platform. Bend your knees to lower the platform towards you, then press back up. Placing your feet too low shifts the work onto the quads and misses the setup.
Leg Press (Narrow Stance): Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet close together on the platform. Bend your knees to lower the platform towards you, then press back up. Letting your knees drift wide instead of tracking straight is the common fault.
Leg Press Calf Raise: Sit in the leg press with your legs extended and the balls of your feet on the platform edge. Press through your feet to extend your ankles, then lower for a full stretch. Bouncing through a short range is the usual fault.
Low Cable Fly: Set both pulleys low, a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent. Sweep your hands up and together in front of your upper chest, then return down and out. Using your legs to throw the handles up takes work off the chest.
Lying Cable Curl: Lie on the floor or a bench facing a low pulley, arms extended towards the machine. Curl the handle up towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows still, then lower slowly. Letting the elbows lift off the floor is the common fault.
Lying Leg Curl: Lie face down on the machine with the pad resting just above your ankles. Curl your heels up towards your glutes, then lower slowly. Lifting your hips off the bench to gain extra range is the usual fault.
Machine Chest Fly (Single-Arm): Sit in the machine with one arm resting on the pad, elbow slightly bent. Bring your arm across your body in an arc until your hand reaches the centre, then return slowly. Using your shoulder to shrug the arm forward is the common fault.
Machine Chest Press: Sit in the machine with the handles level with your chest and your feet flat on the floor. Press the handles forward until your arms extend, then return slowly. Flaring the elbows out wide instead of tracking forward is the common fault.
Machine Crunch: Settle into the machine with the pad set across your chest and your hips held still. Curl your ribs down towards your hips rather than nodding your head forward. Pulling with your neck instead of curling the torso is the usual fault.
Machine Curl: Sit with your arms resting on the pad and your hands gripping the handles. Curl the handles up towards your shoulders, then lower fully slowly. Lifting your elbows off the pad as the set gets harder is the common fault.
Machine Hip Thrust: Lie back into the machine with the pad resting across your hips. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes, then lower slowly. Arching your lower back at the top instead of stopping level is the fault.
Machine Lateral Raise: Sit with your back against the pad and your upper arms against the lever pads. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, then lower slowly. Using momentum to jerk the weight up instead of a smooth raise is the common fault.
Machine Rear Delt Fly: Sit facing the pads with your chest against the support and your arms resting on the handles. Sweep your arms out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Using your upper back to heave the weight is the common fault.
Machine Row (Chest Supported): Sit or lie with your chest against the pad and grip the handles with arms extended. Pull the handles towards your torso, driving your elbows back, then extend slowly. Lifting your chest off the pad to help the pull is the common fault.
Machine Row (Hammer Strength): Sit braced at the machine with your chest supported, gripping the handles with arms extended. Pull the handles towards your torso, driving your elbows back, then extend slowly. Using your torso to heave the weight is the common fault.
Machine Shoulder Press: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles at shoulder height. Press the handles straight up until your arms extend, then lower slowly. Arching your lower back off the pad to help press is the usual fault.
Machine Shoulder Press (Front Delt Focus: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles in front of your shoulders. Press up and slightly forward until your arms extend, then lower slowly. Pressing straight up instead of slightly forward misses the front delts.
Machine Tricep Extension: Sit with your arms resting on the pad, hands gripping the handles, upper arms still. Push the handles down or forward until your arms straighten, then return slowly. Moving at the shoulder instead of just the elbow is the usual mistake.
Machine Y-Raise: Sit facing the pads with your chest against the support and your arms hanging below you. Raise your arms up and out into a Y shape, squeezing your upper back, then lower slowly. Shrugging instead of raising through the arms is the fault.
Neck Extension (Machine): Sit with the pad resting against the back of your head and your neck in a neutral position. Push your head back against the pad, then return slowly to the start. Using your whole upper back to move the pad instead of your neck is the fault.
Neck Flexion (Machine): Sit with the pad resting against your forehead and your neck in a neutral position. Push your head forward against the pad, then return slowly to the start. Using your shoulders to help push instead of just your neck is the common fault.
Neck Harness Extension: Sit or kneel with the harness strapped around your head and a weight hanging behind you. Tilt your head back against the load, then return slowly to neutral. Moving your whole torso instead of just your head is the common fault.
Neck Harness Flexion: Sit or kneel with the harness strapped around your head and a weight hanging in front. Tilt your head forward against the load, then return slowly to neutral. Using your shoulders to help pull the weight is the common fault.
Neck Machine Lateral Flexion: Sit with the side of your head against the pad and your neck in a neutral position. Tilt your head sideways against the pad, then return slowly to the centre. Rushing the reps instead of moving slowly is the usual fault.
Overhead Cable Rope Extension: Stand facing away from a low pulley with a rope held behind your head, elbows pointing up. Extend your arms forward and up until they straighten, then return slowly. Letting the elbows flare out to the sides takes work off the triceps.
Overhead Cable Tricep Extension: Stand facing away from a low pulley, arms bent overhead holding the handle behind your head. Extend your arms up until they straighten, keeping your elbows still, then lower slowly. Letting the elbows drift wide is the common fault.
Pallof Press: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle with both hands against your chest. Press it straight out and hold, without letting your torso twist. Letting your hips or shoulders rotate towards the machine defeats the hold.
Pallof Press (Kneeling): Kneel side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle with both hands against your chest. Press it straight out and hold, without letting your torso twist. Rocking your hips instead of bracing your core is the common fault.
Pec Deck (Machine Fly): Sit with your back against the pad and your forearms resting on the arm pads in front of you. Bring your arms together in front of your chest, then open back out slowly. Letting the weight stack slam down between reps is the common fault.
Pendulum Squat: Set your shoulders against the pad and your feet shoulder width apart on the platform. Bend your knees to lower along the machine's arc, then drive back up. Letting your knees cave inward as you push up is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Chest Press: Sit in the machine with the handles level with your chest, plates loaded evenly on each side. Press the handles forward until your arms extend, then return slowly. Letting one side lead the press unevenly is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Decline Press: Sit in the machine with the seat set so the handles sit level with your lower chest. Press the handles forward and slightly down until your arms extend, then return slowly. Flaring the elbows out wide is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded High Row: Sit or kneel with your chest against the pad, gripping the handles above you. Pull the handles towards your torso, driving your elbows up and back, then extend slowly. Using your torso to heave the weight is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Hip Thrust: Lie back into the machine with the pad across your hips, plates loaded evenly. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes, then lower slowly. Arching your lower back at the top is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Incline Press: Sit in the machine with the seat set so the handles sit level with your upper chest, plates loaded evenly. Press the handles forward and up until your arms extend, then return slowly. Letting one side lead the press is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pads and grip the handles above you, plates loaded evenly. Pull the handles down towards your upper chest, driving your elbows down, then extend slowly. Leaning back excessively is the usual fault.
Plate-Loaded Low Row: Sit with your chest against the pad, feet braced, gripping the handles with arms extended. Pull the handles towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades, then extend back out. Rounding your back at the start is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Overhead Extension: Sit with your arms overhead gripping the handles, plates loaded evenly on the machine. Lower the handles behind your head by bending your elbows, then extend back up. Letting the elbows flare out wide is the usual fault.
Plate-Loaded Preacher Curl: Sit with your arms resting over the preacher pad and grip the handle, plates loaded evenly. Curl the handle up towards your shoulders, then lower fully to extend your arms. Lifting your elbows off the pad is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Rear Delt: Sit facing the pads with your chest against the support, gripping the handles in front of you. Sweep your arms out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Using your upper back to heave the weight is the usual fault.
Plate-Loaded Row: Sit or stand braced at the machine, plates loaded evenly, gripping the handles with arms extended. Pull the handles towards your torso, driving your elbows back, then extend slowly. Leaning back to heave the weight is the common fault.
Plate-Loaded Shoulder Press: Sit with your back against the pad, plates loaded evenly, gripping the handles at shoulder height. Press the handles straight up until your arms extend, then lower slowly. Arching your lower back off the pad is the usual fault.
Preacher Curl Machine: Sit with your arms resting over the preacher pad and your hands gripping the handle. Curl the handle up towards your shoulders, then lower fully to extend your arms. Letting your elbows lift off the pad is the common fault.
Prone Leg Curl: Lie face down on the machine with the pad resting just above your ankles, hips flat against the bench. Curl your heels up towards your glutes, then lower slowly. Lifting your hips off the bench for extra range is the usual fault.
Reverse Cable Crossover: Stand centred between two low pulleys, a handle in each hand with arms crossed in front. Sweep your arms up and out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Swinging your torso to lift the handles is the fault.
Reverse Grip Cable Pushdown: Stand facing a high pulley with an underhand grip on the bar, elbows tucked to your sides. Push the bar down until your arms straighten, then let it rise slowly. Letting the elbows flare out to the sides is the usual fault.
Reverse Hyperextension: Lie face down on a raised bench with your hips at the edge and legs hanging free below. Swing your legs up until your body forms a straight line, using your glutes, then lower slowly. A big swing instead of control is the common fault.
Reverse Hyperextension (Glute): Lie face down on a raised bench with your hips at the edge and legs hanging free below. Drive your legs up by squeezing your glutes until level, then lower slowly. Swinging with momentum instead of a glute drive is the usual fault.
Reverse Pec Deck: Sit facing the pads with your chest against the support, arms on the handles in front. Sweep your arms out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Shrugging instead of squeezing the blades is the common fault.
Rope Pushdown: Stand facing a high pulley with a rope attached, elbows tucked close to your sides. Push the rope down and spread the ends apart as your arms straighten, then return slowly. Letting the elbows drift away from your body is the common fault.
Seated Cable Row: Sit with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, holding the handle with arms extended. Pull it towards your torso, keeping your back upright, then extend back out slowly. Rounding your back to reach further is the common fault.
Seated Calf Raise: Sit with the pad across your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform. Press through your feet to rise onto your toes, pause, then lower for a full stretch. Bouncing through a short range instead of pausing is the usual fault.
Seated Dip Machine: Sit in the machine and grip the handles beside you, feet flat on the floor or footrest. Push the handles down until your arms straighten, then return slowly. Letting the elbows flare out wide is the common fault.
Seated Leg Curl: Sit with the pad resting on top of your shins near your ankles, back flat against the seat. Curl your legs back and down against the resistance, then return slowly. Lifting your hips or thighs off the seat is the usual fault.
Seated Machine Calf Raise: Sit with the pad across your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform edge. Press through your feet to rise onto your toes, pause, then lower for a full stretch. Rushing through short reps instead of pausing is the fault.
Seated Machine Row (Wide): Sit with your feet braced and grip the wide handles with arms extended in front of you. Pull the handles towards your torso, keeping your elbows out wide, then extend back out slowly. Leaning your torso back to help pull is the usual fault.
Seated Rear Delt Machine: Sit facing the pads with your chest against the support, arms resting on the handles in front. Sweep your arms out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Using your upper back to heave the weight is the common fault.
Seated Tibialis Raise: Sit with your heels on a support and the front of your feet under the padded lever. Lift the front of your feet towards your shins against it, then lower slowly. Using your whole leg instead of moving through the ankle is the usual fault.
Serratus Punch: Hold a light handle in one hand, arm extended in front of your chest. Punch your arm further forward by reaching with your shoulder blade, then return slowly. Bending the elbow instead of reaching through the shoulder blade is the fault.
Single Arm Cable Extension: Stand facing away from a low pulley, holding the handle behind your head with one arm, elbow bent. Extend your arm up until it straightens, keeping the elbow tucked, then lower slowly. Letting the elbow flare out is the usual fault.
Single Leg Press: Sit with one foot flat on the centre of the platform and your back flat against the pad. Push through that leg to extend it, then bend your knee to lower slowly. Letting your hip rotate or twist to help push is the common fault.
Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise: Stand side-on to a low pulley, arm hanging across your body holding the handle. Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, leading with the elbow, then lower slowly. Shrugging your shoulder up towards your ear is the usual fault.
Single-Arm Cable Rear Delt Fly: Stand side-on to a pulley, holding the handle across your body with one arm. Sweep your arm out and back to shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blade, then return slowly. Swinging your torso to help move the handle is the common fault.
Single-Arm Cable Row: Sit or stand facing a pulley, holding one handle with arm extended and your torso square. Pull the handle towards your ribs, driving your elbow back, then extend out slowly. Rotating your torso to help pull the handle in is the usual fault.
Single-Arm Cable Woodchop (Standing): Stand side-on to a pulley, holding the handle with one hand away from your body. Rotate through your hips and torso to pull the handle across your body, then return slowly. Bending the arm instead of rotating through the core is the fault.
Single-Arm Cable Wrist Curl: Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing up, holding the handle at your fingertips. Curl your wrist up towards you, then lower it fully to stretch the forearm. Moving your elbow instead of just the wrist is the usual mistake.
Single-Arm Lat Pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pads, grip a single handle above you, arm extended. Pull the handle down to the side of your chest, driving your elbow down, then extend back up. Leaning away from the handle to generate the pull is the fault.
Single-Arm Overhead Cable Extension: Stand facing away from a low pulley, holding the handle overhead with one arm, elbow bent behind your head. Extend your arm up until it straightens, elbow tucked, then lower slowly. Letting the elbow drift out wide is the usual fault.
Sissy Squat Machine: Strap your shins into the machine and hold the handles for support, body upright to start. Lean back and bend your knees until you feel a stretch through your quads, then rise up. Bending at the hips like a squat is the fault.
Smith Machine Bench Press: Lie on a bench under the bar, feet flat on the floor, and unhook it by rotating your wrists. Lower the bar to your chest, then press it back up to straight arms. Setting the bench too far forward or back forces an awkward pressing angle.
Smith Machine Calf Raise: Stand with the bar resting across your upper back and the balls of your feet on a block. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, pause, then lower for a full stretch. Bouncing quickly instead of pausing at the top is the usual mistake.
Smith Machine Close-Grip Press: Lie on a bench under the bar with your hands close together, and unhook it by rotating your wrists. Lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows tucked in, then press back up. Letting the elbows flare out wide is the common fault.
Smith Machine Front Squat: Rack the bar across the front of your shoulders, crossing your arms or using a clean grip, then unhook it. Squat down keeping your torso upright, then drive back up to standing. Letting your elbows drop lets the bar roll forward.
Smith Machine Hip Thrust: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the bar across your hips, feet flat. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line, then lower slowly. Arching at the top instead of stopping level is the common fault.
Smith Machine Incline Press: Set the bench to a shallow incline under the bar and lie back, unhooking the bar by rotating your wrists. Lower it to your upper chest, then press back up to straight arms. A bench angled too steep shifts work onto the shoulders.
Smith Machine Row: Sit or stand braced under the bar set at hip height, holding it with an underhand or overhand grip. Pull the bar towards your torso, driving your elbows back, then extend slowly. Leaning back excessively to help the pull is the usual fault.
Smith Machine Shrug: Stand holding the bar at hip height, arms straight, and unhook it from the rack. Shrug your shoulders straight up towards your ears, then lower slowly. Rolling the shoulders instead of moving straight up and down is the common fault.
Smith Machine Squat: Rack the bar across your upper back, feet slightly forward of the bar path, then unhook it. Squat down keeping your torso upright, then drive back up to standing. Feet directly under the bar fights the fixed path.
Standing Cable Chest Press (Single-Arm): Stand facing away from a low pulley with one foot forward, holding the handle at chest height with one arm. Press the handle forward until your arm extends, then return slowly. Rotating your torso to add power is the fault.
Standing Calf Raise (Machine): Set your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the platform, standing upright. Rise onto your toes as high as possible, pause, then lower for a full stretch. Bouncing through a short range instead of pausing is the mistake.
Standing Leg Curl: Stand at the machine with the pad resting behind one ankle, hips square and torso upright. Curl your heel up towards your glute against the resistance, then lower slowly. Leaning forward and using hip momentum is the common fault.
Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press: Kneel upright with your hips fully extended, side-on to a cable at chest height, the handle against your chest. Press it straight out and hold, without letting your hips sway. Letting your torso rotate towards the machine is the fault.
Tib Bar Raise (Machine): Sit with your heels resting on a support and the front of your feet hooked under the bar. Pull your toes up towards your shins against the resistance, then lower slowly. Rushing through the reps instead of moving slowly is the common fault.
Tricep Pushdown (Bar): Stand facing a high pulley with a straight bar attached, elbows tucked close to your sides. Push the bar down until your arms straighten, then let it rise slowly. Letting the elbows drift away from your sides is the usual fault.
Tricep Pushdown (Rope): Stand facing a high pulley with a rope attached, leaning slightly forward, elbows pinned to your sides. Push the rope down, splitting the ends apart, then let it rise slowly. Leaning on the stack, not your triceps, is the fault.
Triceps Extension Machine: Sit with your arm resting along the pad, hand gripping the handle, upper arm still. Push the handle down or forward until your arm straightens, then return slowly. Moving at the shoulder instead of the elbow is the usual mistake.
V-Bar Pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pads and grip the V-shaped handle, palms facing each other. Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back, then extend back up. Leaning back excessively is the common fault.
Viking Press: Sit or stand gripping the handles with a neutral grip in front of your chest. Press the handles straight up overhead until your arms extend, then lower slowly. Leaning back excessively to help press the weight up is the usual mistake.
Wide-Grip Cable Row: Sit with your feet on the platform and take a wide bar attachment, arms extended with a tall spine. Pull the bar towards your torso with elbows out wide, then extend back out slowly. Rounding your back at the start is the common fault.
